channel.title: RegTrac Briefs
channel.description: Per-regulator briefs on India's statutory financial regulators.

item.title: Small Industries Development Bank of India — what changed, and what to watch
item.description: SIDBI: MSME development finance, deliberately not a conduct regulator.

item.title: Securities and Exchange Board of India — what changed, and what to watch
item.description: SEBI: The markets regulator. Everything listed, everything pooled, everything sold as an investment: brokers, mutual funds, AIFs, IPOs, takeover codes, insider trading. SEBI writes the rules…

item.title: Reserve Bank of India — what changed, and what to watch
item.description: RBI: The oldest and most powerful financial regulator in India — and the one that touches the most people. The RBI licenses and supervises banks, NBFCs and payment systems, sets interest-rate policy…

item.title: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority — what changed, and what to watch
item.description: PFRDA: The youngest of the big-four regulators. PFRDA runs the National Pension System and Atal Pension Yojana — the retirement money of government employees, since 2004, and any citizen who opts in.…

item.title: National Payments Corporation of India — what changed, and what to watch
item.description: NPCI: Everyone assumes it is a regulator. It is not: NPCI is a Section 8 company that runs UPI.

item.title: National Housing Bank — what changed, and what to watch
item.description: NHB: Built to grow housing finance, then stripped of the rulebook it was built around.

item.title: National Financial Reporting Authority — what changed, and what to watch
item.description: NFRA: Audit oversight with real enforcement teeth and no door for the public.

item.title: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development — what changed, and what to watch
item.description: NABARD: Part development bank, part supervisor. NABARD refinances rural credit and runs India's farm-infrastructure funds — and, less visibly, carries statutory supervisory duties over cooperative…

item.title: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India — what changed, and what to watch
item.description: IRDAI: The policyholder's regulator — in theory. IRDAI licenses insurers and intermediaries, approves products, and sits on top of grievance machinery (Bima Bharosa, insurance ombudsmen) that handles…

item.title: International Financial Services Centres Authority — what changed, and what to watch
item.description: IFSCA: India's youngest and most unusual regulator: one authority, all sectors, one square kilometre. Since 1 October 2020, IFSCA has replaced RBI, SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA inside GIFT City — banking…

item.title: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India — what changed, and what to watch
item.description: IBBI: The regulator for the end of the corporate life cycle: insolvency professionals, their agencies, information utilities, and the process rules under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. For…

item.title: Financial Stability and Development Council — what changed, and what to watch
item.description: FSDC: The apex body where regulators meet the Finance Minister — with no statute, and largely unpublished minutes.

item.title: Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation — what changed, and what to watch
item.description: DICGC: The backstop nobody thinks about until a bank fails: a Rs 5 lakh promise standing behind every deposit.
